title: Which of these are supervised learning problems?
prompt: Cartwheel's teams have pitched five ideas. Select every idea that is a **supervised learning** problem: one where you have past examples with a known answer and want a model to predict that answer for new cases.
hints: Ask of each idea: is there a column of known answers in the historical data?
Supervised covers both categories (classification) and numbers (regression).
One idea has no labels at all, and one is a rule someone can already write down.
explanation: Churn flags, next-year spend and ticket routing all have historical answers to learn from: two classification problems and one regression problem. Finding shopping styles has no labels, so it is unsupervised clustering. The $10,000 review threshold is a known rule, so it needs an `if`, not a model.

churn-flag.text: Predict whether a customer will order again in the next 90 days, using past customers whose outcome is known.
churn-flag.why: Supervised classification: the historical `churned` column is the label.

spend-next-year.text: Predict how much a customer will spend next year, using customers from previous years.
spend-next-year.why: Supervised regression: past customers' actual spend is a numeric label.

find-segments.text: Discover a handful of shopping styles among customers, without any predefined styles.
find-segments.why: No labels exist, so this is unsupervised learning (clustering).

big-order-rule.text: Flag every order above $10,000 for manual review.
big-order-rule.why: The rule is known and exact. Write the condition; no learning is involved.

ticket-team.text: Route each new support ticket to one of five teams, using past tickets that were routed correctly.
ticket-team.why: Supervised multi-class classification: past routing decisions are the labels.
